technique_name: Explain the differences between two given data structures
description: Arrays and linked lists are both linear data structures, but they differ in several important ways. Arrays store data items at contiguous memory locations and use indexes to access the items. The items in an array must be of the same type, and can be accessed in constant time. Linked lists, on the other hand, store data items at non-contiguous memory locations and use links to access the items.
